s that test size:
- `importBackup` rejects when `file.size > MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` (`app/backup.js:123`). I passed it a real `Blob` holding the text, with a store whose `replace` returns `'saved'`.
- `tooBigToImport(text)` counts the UTF-8 bytes of the text (`app/backup.js:82-84`). I called it directly on the same text.

Each test file is a valid backup made with `toBackupText` and padded to an exact byte count. If the size check passes, the file goes through the full import. I padded it two ways: with trailing spaces, and with 3-byte `€` characters in a title. The second way makes the character count very different from the byte count, so it shows the limit is counted in bytes.

**What I saw**

| Case | Bytes | `Blob.size` | `tooBigToImport` | `importBackup` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spaces, limit − 1 | 1,048,575 | 1,048,575 | false | Accepted: "Đã nhập 1 việc." |
| Spaces, limit | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 | false | Accepted: "Đã nhập 1 việc." |
| Spaces, limit + 1 | 1,048,577 | 1,048,577 | true | Rejected: `fileTooBig` |
| `€` title, limit (349,610 chars) | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 | false | Accepted |
| `€` title, limit + 1 (349,611 chars) | 1,048,577 | 1,048,577 | true | Rejected |

`MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` is 1048576. Both checks use `>`, so a file of exactly the limit is accepted and the first byte over is rejected. The limit counts bytes, not characters: about 350,000 three-byte characters already reach it.

Nothing under `app/` or `tests/` was changed, and I didn't run `node --test`.
